old: Old medicine imagined the body sending trouble off to gather in one spot, like guests shown to a separate room.
Its Latin ancestor literally meant 'a going away.'
It's built from the same Latin root as 'cede' — the idea of departing or withdrawing.
clues: This bodily ailment takes its name from a Latin word that meant both 'a going away' and 'a gathering of humors.'
A painful, swollen pocket of pus caused by infection. Unlike a simple cyst, it usually needs draining, since ancient doctors believed bad humors withdrew and collected there.
Dentists treat the tooth kind with antibiotics or a root canal. The word is a cousin of cede, sharing a Latin root meaning 'go.'
